items.body:
Brad White pressure packages — simulated looks, JACK triggers, and coverage match rules.

Concept
Pressure Package: Coordinated extra rushers or simulated pressures to force quick throws or negative run plays.
• Five-man pressure looks without always sending five
• JACK is primary trigger
• Coverage must match pressure call
Strengths: Disrupts timing; Creates negative plays; Forces hot throws
Weaknesses: Exposes man coverage if rush doesn't arrive
Examples: Brad White simulated pressures; Third-down package tendencies

UF Scheme Usage
Unit: defense
Simulated and five-man pressures triggered from JACK and STAR in package downs.
Notes: Coverage must match pressure look — no free shots.
Frequency: 70% of install

items.body:
At FSU — RPO quick game, TE red-zone usage, and rivalry-game field-position keys.

Concept
RPO Quick Game: Run-pass option where the quarterback reads a conflict defender post-snap and distributes to run or quick pass.
• Stress conflict players in odd fronts
• Tempo limits defensive substitution
• Ball must come out on time vs pressure
Strengths: Puts conflict on defense; Efficient with tempo; High-percentage throws
Weaknesses: Requires QB discipline; Turnover risk on late reads
Examples: FAU spread-RPO attack; UF offense packaged RPO elements

UF Scheme Usage

Notes: Jayden Woods at JACK, Kanye Clark at STAR, Brendan Bett at nose.
Frequency: 95% of install

Notes: Field position and turnover margin decide rivalry games.

items.body:
Mesh concept in UF's spread passing menu — route spacing, zone reads, and WR traits.

Concept
Mesh Concept: Two shallow crossing routes from opposite directions designed to create natural rubs in zone coverage.
• Read zone drop depth
• Timing between crossers is critical
• Often paired with vertical routes
Strengths: Free receiver vs zone; High-percentage intermediate throw
Weaknesses: Man coverage with trail technique can eliminate rub
Examples: Spread passing install; Vertical passing package complement

UF Scheme Usage
Unit: offense
Mesh and vertical concepts in spread passing menu.
Notes: Rebuilt OL protection is swing factor for downfield shots.
Frequency: 60% of install

Recruiting Fit
Position: WR
Spread RPO offense needs receivers who win with route running and speed on vertical and mesh concepts.
Body type: 6-0 to 6-3, 185–210 lbs
Technical: Route tree proficiency; Separation at break point

Position Traits
Route Running (WR): Release, stem, break sharpness, and separation at top of routes.
Speed (WR): Top-end straight-line speed in open field.

How Brad White's 3-3-5 odd front works at Florida — personnel, JACK/STAR roles, and why it fits modern spread offenses.

Concept
3-3-5 Defense: Three down linemen, three linebackers, and five defensive backs — with hybrid edge (JACK) and nickel (STAR) roles.
• Odd front frees five defenders to flow to the ball
• Personnel-driven answer to spread offenses
• Edge integrity and STAR communication are early diagnostics

Weaknesses: Requires hybrid talent at JACK/STAR; Can be stressed by heavy run fits if nose is controlled

items.body:
JACK linebacker in the UF 3-3-5 — edge setting, pass rush, and the traits required to play the spot.

Concept
JACK Linebacker: Hybrid edge defender who sets the edge, rushes the passer, and can drop into short zone coverage.
• Centerpiece of Brad White's pressure package
• Must set edge before rushing
• Convert speed to power through contact
Strengths: Pass-rush flexibility; Edge setting; Coverage versatility
Weaknesses: High physical and mental demand; Exposed if edge is lost
Examples: Jayden Woods as scheme centerpiece at JACK; Edge set vs FAU tempo attack

UF Scheme Usage
Unit: defense
JACK is the scheme centerpiece — edge setting and pass rush both run through this hybrid spot.
Notes: Primary blitzer and edge setter in the odd front.
Frequency: 90% of install

Recruiting Fit
Position: JACK
JACK in Brad White's 3-3-5 requires edge burst, block shedding, and speed-to-power.
Body type: 6-2 to 6-4, 230–250 lbs, long arms preferred
Technical: Edge setting; Block shed; Pass-rush plan

Position Traits
Burst (JACK): Explosive first-step acceleration off the snap.
Block Shedding (JACK): Hand usage and leverage to disengage from blockers.
Speed to Power (JACK): Ability to convert speed into power through contact at the edge.

STAR/nickel in the 3-3-5 — slot coverage, run fits, and why tempo offenses test this position first.

Concept
STAR / Nickel: Hybrid nickel who covers slot receivers, fits the run from depth, and blitzes in package downs.
• Primary matchup piece vs 11 personnel
• Must communicate run/pass conflict
• Fit and finish in space
Strengths: Slot coverage; Run support from depth; Blitz package flexibility
Weaknesses: Size mismatch vs big slot bodies if undersized
Examples: Kanye Clark projects at STAR in 2026; STAR fit tested early vs tempo teams

Technical: Slot coverage; Run fit from depth; Communication
